LEGAL_EFFECT: priority treatment of trusted flaggers' notices
RATIONALE: Obligation on the target; the intermediary is the beneficiary of the priority rule.

TEXT_SPAN: notices submitted by trusted flaggers, acting within their designated area of expertise, through the mechanisms referred to in Article 16
ACTION_ADDRESSEE: Providers of online platforms (via the Article 16 notice mechanisms)
TRIGGER_CONDITION: acting within their designated area of expertise
RATIONALE: Submitting notices is presupposed (participial clause), not imposed. Detecting and notifying illegal content (cf. 22(2)(a)) = tracking risks/conduct → monitoring; the core activity is transmission of information to the target. REV has no 'reporting/flagging' function (calibration item).

TEXT_SPAN: The status of ‘trusted flagger’ under this Regulation shall be awarded, upon application by any entity, by the Digital Services Coordinator of the Member State in which the applicant is established
ACTOR: the Digital Services Coordinator of the Member State in which the applicant is established
TRIGGER_CONDITION: upon application by any entity; applicant has demonstrated conditions (a)-(c)
RATIONALE: Recognition by a public authority after demonstration of conditions = vetting.

TEXT_SPAN: it has particular expertise and competence for the purposes of detecting, identifying and notifying illegal content;
OBJECT: detecting, identifying and notifying illegal content
RATIONALE: Condition of recognition; also states the activity profile (detect, identify, notify).

TEXT_SPAN: Trusted flaggers shall publish, at least once a year easily comprehensible and detailed reports on notices submitted in accordance with Article 16 during the relevant period.
OBJECT: reports on notices (by provider, type of content, action taken by the provider)
RATIONALE: Transparency/reporting obligation on the intermediary (REV ¶85: transparency_disclosure / reporting).

TEXT_SPAN: Trusted flaggers shall send those reports to the awarding Digital Services Coordinator, and shall make them publicly available.
OBJECT: reports on notices, including the action taken by providers
TARGET_ACTOR: providers of hosting services (whose actions are reported)
RATIONALE: Transmission to the oversight body of information that includes the targets' responses. Under the unrevised definition this is monitoring ('…transmitting information to an oversight body'); under REV it is primarily a reporting/notification obligation. Kept as a calibration item.

TEXT_SPAN: Digital Services Coordinators shall communicate to the Commission and the Board the names, addresses and email addresses of the entities to which they have awarded the status of the trusted flagger
OBJECT: identity of entities awarded (or suspended/revoked) trusted flagger status

TEXT_SPAN: The Commission shall publish the information referred to in paragraph 4 in a publicly available database, in an easily accessible and machine-readable format, and shall keep the database up to date.
ACTION: shall publish and keep up to date

TEXT_SPAN: it shall communicate that information to the Digital Services Coordinator that awarded the status of trusted flagger to the entity concerned, providing the necessary explanations and supporting documents.
ACTION_ADDRESSEE: the Digital Services Coordinator that awarded the status
OBJECT: information on insufficiently precise, inaccurate or inadequately substantiated notices
TRIGGER_CONDITION: Where a provider of online platforms has information indicating that a trusted flagger has submitted a significant number of insufficiently precise, inaccurate or inadequately substantiated notices
RATIONALE: Target reports on the intermediary to the regulator: the intermediary is the object of oversight.

TEXT_SPAN: the status of trusted flagger shall be suspended during the period of the investigation
REGULATOR_ACTOR: Digital Services Coordinator (forms the triggering view)
TRIGGER_CONDITION: Upon receiving the information from the provider of online platforms, and if the Digital Services Coordinator considers that there are legitimate reasons to open an investigation
RATIONALE: Legal effect; the suspending actor is not named.

TEXT_SPAN: The Digital Services Coordinator that awarded the status of trusted flagger to an entity shall revoke that status if it determines, following an investigation either on its own initiative or on the basis information received from third parties, including the information provided by a provider of online platforms pursuant to paragraph 6, that the entity no longer meets the conditions set out in paragraph 2.
ACTOR: The Digital Services Coordinator that awarded the status
TRIGGER_CONDITION: if it determines, following an investigation ..., that the entity no longer meets the conditions set out in paragraph 2

TEXT_SPAN: Before revoking that status, the Digital Services Coordinator shall afford the entity an opportunity to react to the findings of its investigation and its intention to revoke the entity’s status as trusted flagger.
ACTION: shall afford an opportunity to react

TEXT_SPAN: The Commission, after consulting the Board, shall, where necessary, issue guidelines to assist providers of online platforms and Digital Services Coordinators in the application of paragraphs 2, 6 and 7.
ACTION_ADDRESSEE: providers of online platforms and Digital Services Coordinators
TRIGGER_CONDITION: where necessary; after consulting the Board
